## Description

`build_genesis_artifacts_with_manifest` in `crates/ol/genesis/src/lib.rs` constructs `OLParams::default()` without setting `last_l1_block`. The field exists on OLParams for exactly this purpose but was never populated. This leaves `last_l1_height = 0` in the genesis OL state. When the first terminal block is built, block assembly calls `fetch_asm_manifests_from(1)`, which fails because the ASM only has manifests from the actual genesis L1 height (110) onward. Non-terminal blocks don't fetch manifests, so existing tests (which never reach a terminal block) pass fine.

payload.body:
## Description

<!--
Provide a brief summary of the changes and the motivation behind them.
-->
This PR rearranges the fields in `GameData` (needed for graph generation) to reflect when each field is available (deposit-time vs setup-time vs genesis-time). It then updates the `GraphState` to only store the deposit-time values and adds helpers to `GraphSMCfg` and `GraphSMCtx` to make it easier to get to the `GameData` type expected by the graph generation API.

Note that all the keys are assumed to be static over the lifetime of the bridge. However, some of these may need to be queried and verified via Mosaic. Stake is assumed to be scoped to a single graph in order to support multiple stakes per operator (just in case).

Storing the `DepositParams` gives us storage/memory efficiency (~10x for 10 watchtowers) by trading off some computation cost. On an M4 Max, a single graph generation, with 10 watchtowers and 160 proof bytes (as per the test configuration in the `tx-graph2::game_graph` module), takes around 150 ms in debug mode and <10 ms in release mode, which makes this tradeoff acceptable.

As a cleanup step, this PR also adds `GraphIdx` to the `GraphSMCtx` to replace the `operator_idx` and `deposit_idx` fields. The getters for these sub-fields have been retained for convenience.

Copilot was used for autocompletion.

payload.title: fix(asm): make AuxRequestCollector bounds-aware to prevent DoS
payload.body:
## Description

      A malicious L1 transaction tagged as a checkpoint can claim an arbitrary
      L1 height (e.g. 999999). The old AuxRequestCollector blindly forwarded
      this to the aux resolver, which failed on non-existent manifest hashes
      blocking processing of the entire L1 block and stalling the ASM.

      Make the collector bounds-aware by passing the accumulator's last
      inserted height at construction. Requests for ranges beyond this bound
      or with inverted start/end are silently dropped. Invalid payloads are
      still rejected during process_txs validation.

Fixes current issue with previous epoch always being null. The following needed to be done for the fix:

payload.title: refactor(net): extract API types into net-svc-api crate
payload.body:
## Summary

Two changes in this PR:

1. **Extract the public API surface from `net-svc` into a new `net-svc-api` crate** (#74) — lets consumers like the SM Scheduler depend only on API types without pulling in the full QUIC/TLS implementation.
2. **Extend integration test deadlines to 2 minutes** (#95) — the net-svc and net-client tests had 3–20s deadlines that pass locally but fail on slow CI runners.

Also removes the unused `crates/network/api` crate.

---

## 1. `net-svc-api` extraction

### What moved to `net-svc-api`

| Module | Types |
|--------|-------|
| `peer_id` | `PeerId`, `peer_id_from_signing_key`, `peer_id_from_verifying_key` |
| `config` | `NetServiceConfig`, `PeerConfig` |
| `api` | `Stream`, `StreamClosed`, `PayloadBuf`, `NetServiceHandle`, `BulkTransferExpectation`, `OpenStreamError`, `ExpectError` |
| `api` (hidden) | `StreamRequest`, `NetCommand` — `#[doc(hidden)]`, shared between api and svc backend |

### What stays in `net-svc`

- `NetService`, `NetServiceController` — service lifecycle
- `tls` — cert generation, `PeerVerifier`, QUIC config helpers
- `svc/` — connection management, stream handling, reconnect logic
- `close_codes` — QUIC-internal VarInt constants (not surfaced in API)

### Dependency graph after

```
SM Scheduler ──────► net-svc-api
                         ▲
                         │
net-client ──────────────┤
                         │
net-svc ─────────────────┘
```

### Backwards compatibility

`net-svc` re-exports all moved modules

payload.title: feat(job): implement network action handlers
payload.body:
## Summary

Implements the network send+ack job handlers and consolidates `PeerId` as a proper newtype. Stacks on #73.

## Network Action Handlers

Four handlers that send protocol messages via `net-client` and return the corresponding `ActionResult` to the SM:

| Role | Action | Result |
|------|--------|--------|
| Garbler | `SendCommitMsgChunk` | `CommitMsgChunkAcked` |
| Garbler | `SendChallengeResponseMsgChunk` | `ChallengeResponseChunkAcked` |
| Evaluator | `SendChallengeMsg` | `ChallengeMsgAcked` |
| Evaluator | `DepositSendAdaptorMsgChunk` | `DepositAdaptorChunkSent` |

Each handler retries in a loop until the send succeeds — transient disconnections are logged with `tracing::warn!` (with structured context: wire/circuit/chunk index) and retried. The `net-client` send includes its own `open_timeout` and `ack_timeout`, so each retry iteration isn't a spin.

## PeerId Newtype

Replaces the old `mosaic_common::PeerId(Vec<u8>)` stub with a proper newtype in `net-svc-api`:

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct PeerId([u8; 32]);
```

- Type-safe — can't accidentally pass an arbitrary `[u8; 32]`
- `from_bytes`/`as_bytes`/`to_bytes` accessors
- `Display` (hex), `Debug` (`PeerId(hex)`), `Ord`, `Hash`, `Serialize`, `Deserialize`
- `From<[u8; 32]>`, `TryFrom<&[u8]>` conversions

All crates now import `PeerId` from `mosaic-net-svc-api`. Crates that only depended on `mosaic-common` for `PeerId` (`rpc/api`, `rpc/ser

payload.title: feat(job): implement polynomial/share generation and verification handlers
payload.body:
## Summary

Implements three setup-phase job handlers and introduces a polynomial cache. Stacks on #96 → #73.

## Handlers

| Action | Side | What it does |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `GeneratePolynomialCommitments(Seed)` | Garbler | Generates ~240 MB polynomials from seed, caches them, computes EC commitments (~44s of scalar multiplications) |
| `GenerateShares(Seed, Index)` | Garbler | Reads cached polynomials, evaluates all wire/value polynomials at circuit index, returns input + output shares |
| `VerifyOpenedInputShares` | Evaluator | Verifies 174 × 172 × 256 = ~7.7M opened shares against polynomial commitments. Returns `None` on success, `Some(reason)` on first failure |

Reference implementations: Manish's `job_generate_polynomial_commitments` and `job_generate_shares_for_index` from `feat_stf/job_pseudocode_draft`.

## Polynomial Cache

Polynomials are ephemeral — generated once during setup, used to produce commitments and shares, then discarded. They never need to be persisted.

The cache avoids regenerating ~240 MB of polynomials 181 times (once per `GenerateShares` call):

- **Keyed by `Seed`** (32 bytes) — pure memoization, same seed always produces same polynomials
- **Holds `Arc<AllPolynomials>`** — concurrent `GenerateShares` workers share the same data without copying
- **Auto-evicts** after `N_CIRCUITS` (181) reads — deterministic, no timers
- **`max_entries = 4`** — caps memory at ~960 MB (4 concurrent peer setups)
- **Cache miss fallback** — regener

payload.title: Prague Testnet Readiness and Public Testing Plan
payload.body_md:
## Highlights

Prague testnet support is now in place behind a guarded testnet profile across `product:strata` and `product:strata-bridge`. The main point of the week was not just getting Prague parameters wired in, but making sure we can expose them without turning every downstream repo into a one-off configuration fork. `person:prajwolrg` drove the thread end to end and kept the protocol-side scope tight while the endpoint names and infra rollout window were still moving.

The guarded profile gives us a clean boundary: Prague-specific constants, service endpoints, bridge assumptions, and public testing defaults are isolated from the current stable testnet path. That matters because we still have several surfaces that consume the same network facts differently: `repo:alpen`, `repo:strata-bridge`, `repo:strata-p2p`, `repo:checkpoint-explorer`, `repo:alpen-dashboards`, and `repo:alpen-faucet`. The work this week reduced configuration drift rather than spreading another set of copied values across the stack.

The biggest constraint was sequencing. Bridge validation depended on infra stability landing late in the window, and public docs plus faucet readiness trailed the core protocol changes. `person:krsnapaudel` handled the staged rollout under a narrower-than-planned window because infra maintenance compressed the available test period. Endpoint naming also changed twice, which delayed the external testing note until the final names were settled.

## What shipped

Prague support shipped behind the guarded testnet profile. The profile now gives us a controlled way to run Prague-specific nodes, P2P settings, and bridge paths without making it the default for unrelated testnet users. `person:MdTeach` helped tighten the protocol assumptions around the profile so the change stays explicit and reviewable instead of relying on ambient environment behavior.

The staged rollout path is now usable. `person:krsnapaudel` coordinated the infra side so we could bring up the pieces in order, verify health, and avoid publishing unstable endpoint names. This included the practical cleanup around endpoint naming after the second change, which was annoying but necessary: external testers should see stable names once, not track our internal churn.

Bridge validation made it through the critical path. `person:Rajil1213` and `person:ProofOfKeags` worked through the bridge-facing pieces in `repo:strata-bridge`, including the places where validation depends on the final infra shape rather than just protocol constants. The result is not “bridge is done forever”; it is that the Prague profile now has enough validated bridge behavior to support controlled public testing.

The public testing note is drafted around final endpoint names. I held the external note until the endpoint names stopped changing, then aligned the language with the actual rollout state rather than overpromising. `person:john-light` owns getting that note out with the faucet and dashboard caveats clearly called out.

`repo:checkpoint-explorer`, `repo:alpen-dashboards`, and `repo:alpen-faucet` are not the pacing items for core protocol readiness, but they are pacing items for public tester experience. This week made that distinction explicit. We can run Prague internally; for public testers, faucet availability, dashboard labels, and explorer links need to be accurate enough that they do not create support load immediately.

## Coming up

Next step is to finish the public testing path, not just the protocol path. That means confirming final endpoint names in every public-facing place, checking faucet behavior against the Prague profile, and making sure dashboard and explorer references point at the right network.

We also need one more pass on cross-repo configuration drift. The guarded profile helps, but it does not automatically prove every consumer is reading the same source of truth. The remaining risk is silent mismatch: one repo using updated Prague parameters while another still points at an older endpoint or stale chain configuration.

For bridge work, the next useful milestone is repeatable validation under expected public-test conditions. We should test with the same endpoint names, faucet path, and docs that external testers will use. Otherwise we only prove that the internal setup works when operated by people who already know the system.

Public docs should stay deliberately narrow. The first Prague testing note should tell testers what is ready, what is guarded, and what failure reports we actually want. It should not imply production readiness or general-purpose network stability.

## Q&A summary

The main question was whether Prague support should be treated as generally available once the guarded profile landed. Answer: no. The profile is ready for controlled testnet exposure, but we are still gating public testing on endpoint stability, bridge validation confidence, and the faucet/docs path.

There was also discussion about why endpoint names were allowed to change this late. The short version is that infra maintenance compressed the rollout window and forced us to settle naming only after the staged deployment shape was clear. That cost us time, but publishing unstable names would have created worse downstream cleanup.

Another question was whether public docs should wait for faucet and dashboard polish. The answer is to publish only when the basic tester loop is coherent. We do not need polished dashboards to begin testing, but we do need testers to know where to connect, how to get funds, what bridge behavior is expected, and where to report failures.

On bridge readiness, the answer remains practical: Prague bridge validation is far enough along for controlled testing, but we should keep watching infra-dependent behavior closely. The bridge path is where late infra instability is most likely to show up as confusing user-facing failures.

## Shoutouts

Shoutout to `person:prajwolrg` for driving the thread across protocol, bridge, infra, and docs without letting the scope sprawl.

Shoutout to `person:krsnapaudel` for getting the staged rollout through a narrowed infra window and keeping endpoint naming grounded in the actual deployment.

Shoutout to `person:MdTeach` for tightening the protocol-side profile work and helping keep Prague behavior explicit.

Shoutout to `person:Rajil1213` and `person:ProofOfKeags` for pushing bridge validation forward despite depending on late infra stability.

Shoutout to `person:bewakes` for helping keep protocol review pressure on the right surfaces.

Shoutout to `person:john-light` for holding the external testing note until the final endpoint names were real, then turning the rollout state into tester-facing guidance.

payload.body:
## Summary

Complete implementation of the Mosaic job system: all 18 action handlers, three execution pools, multi-threaded garbling coordinator with shared circuit reader, and production-grade retry/eviction handling.

## What's in this PR

### All 18 Handler Implementations

Every garbler (G1–G10) and evaluator (E1–E8) action handler is implemented and cross-checked against Manish's reference code in PR #68. Algorithms verified for:
- RNG derivation order (ChaCha20 deterministic seeding)
- Share truncation, polynomial commitment/evaluation, FreeXOR garbling
- Adaptor generate/verify/complete/extract_share with correct sighash indexing
- Commitment format: `blake3(ct_hash ‖ translate_hash ‖ output_label_ct)`
- E8 share interpolation, label translation, circuit evaluation

### Three Execution Pools

| Pool | Model | Purpose |
|------|-------|---------|
| **Light** | FIFO, 1 thread, 32 concurrency | Network I/O (sends, acks, E4 bulk receive) |
| **Heavy** | Priority queue, 2 threads, 8 concurrency | CPU crypto (polynomial ops, verification, adaptors) |
| **Garbling** | Multi-threaded coordinator | Coordinated sequential reads of ~130 GB circuit file |

Priority: Critical (withdrawal) > High (deposit) > Normal (setup).

### Multi-Threaded Garbling Coordinator

The coordinator solves the shared reader problem: concurrent readers at different offsets cause disk thrashing. One sequential read serves N concurrent sessions.

payload.title: feat!(admin-tx): add tagged sighash for multisig actions
payload.body:
## Description

<!--
Provide a brief summary of the changes and the motivation behind them.
-->
The previous sighash was `SHA256(borsh_hash(action) ‖ seqno)`, which relied on Borsh's internal tagging (enum discriminants, field ordering) for domain separation. This is fragile: reordering enum variants, adding/removing fields, or restructuring types silently changes the sighash. 

The explicit payload layout also makes it straightforward to compute the sighash in other languages (TypeScript, Python, Go, etc.) without needing a Borsh implementation — any language with SHA-256 and byte concatenation can reproduce the hash.

* Replace bare `TxType` constants with a `repr(u8)` `AdminTxType` enum that is the single source of truth for admin transaction type discriminants.
* Introduce a `Sighash` trait that each action type implements, providing domain-separated tagged hashes `(SHA256(SHA256(tag) ‖ seqno ‖ payload))`.
* Each `AdminTxType` variant has a unique BIP-340–style sighash tag (strata/admin/<variant>) with lazy-computed tag hashes
* Simplify test harness by having `build_envelope_tx` accept a `TagData` directly and having `AdminContext::sign` return only the payload

This PR implements the core Checkpoint Proof Statement logic, covering two major bindings:

payload.title: impl Orchestrator for Bridge
payload.body:
## Description

<!--
Provide a brief summary of the changes and the motivation behind them.
-->
This PR implements the Orchestrator for the bridge based on the design doc (but with some deviations from it for practical reasons). The entire crate is implemented as a pipeline of following components:

- *EventsMux*: for subscribing to events and multiplexing them into a `UnifiedEvent` stream for consumption downstream.
- *EventsRouter*: for mapping events to specific state machine IDs (`SMId` wrapper is created for this).
- *SignalsRouter*: for mapping signals emitted by STFs to other state machines.
- *EventsClassifier*: for mapping external events to those expected by SMs.
- *SMRegistry*: an in-memory cache of all state machines in the bridge for actually running STFs.

payload.body:
## Description

This PR is a full net-svc soundness alignment + test hardening pass on top of `origin/main` (`+3730 / -887`, 21 files).

It implements the soundness model in code, stabilizes cancellation/lifecycle behavior, and hardens the net test infrastructure that was causing CI flakes.

Key changes:
- Implemented explicit per-peer connection FSM in net-svc (`Idle`, `ConnectingOutbound`, `ActiveStable`, `Race`) with deterministic simultaneous-connect convergence via lower-peer-ID tie-break.
- Added overlap-key based race evidence and generation-based stale-event isolation in service state/handlers/tasks.
- Reworked stream-open lifecycle to explicit request tracking:
  - request IDs
  - `Pending` / `InFlight` request state
  - explicit `CancelOpen { request_id }`
  - cancel registry + deterministic cleanup on completion/loss/replacement
- Removed implicit receiver-count cancellation correctness paths; cancellation is now explicit and request-scoped.
- Added overlap-key validation handling and close-code coverage for invalid overlap metadata.
- Added/updated security model docs in TLS and a formal spec doc:
  - `crates/net/svc/docs/connection-soundness-model.md`
- Reworked integration/minimal test suites to reduce flakiness:
  - cross-process port allocator for net tests
  - bounded controller shutdown helpers (prevents teardown hangs)
  - reduced fixed sleeps in favor of event-driven waits/retries
  - hardened historically flaky tests (`ack`, `drop wi

payload.body:
## Description

<!--
Provide a brief summary of the changes and the motivation behind them.
-->
This PR reverts the commit that replaced github runners with self-hosted ones. This is because when there are multiple CI jobs running concurrently, the runner becomes under-resourced (even with 16 cores as of this PR). Each such run builds the required binaries where `rustc` uses as many cores as available. This causes functional tests to fail at the setup phase itself (spawning nodes, generating bitcoin blocks, etc.). Github runners are isolated environments where such issues do not occur.

A caching step for openssl has also been added to speed up CI builds a bit.

Codex was used for the caching script (third commit and fourth commits). Claude was used to simplify the script (in the last commit).

payload.title: fix(functional-tests): handle sequencer forwarding race in fullnode tx submission
payload.body:
## Summary
- **Root cause**: `_SharedDevAccount` used module-level global nonce counters shared across all tests and environments. When tests in different envs (`alpen_ee`, `alpen_ee_multi`) both called `sync_nonce()`, they interfered with each other's state. Combined with a race condition in the fullnode's tx forwarding path (forward to sequencer → local pool add), this caused intermittent `"already known"` errors on resource-constrained merge queue runners.
- **Fix 1** — `accounts.py`: Removed `_SharedDevAccount` and all module-level globals. `get_dev_account(rpc)` now requires an RPC client and auto-syncs nonce from chain state. Each call returns a fresh `ManagedAccount` with its own nonce counter. Future test authors can't forget `sync_nonce()` because it's built into the factory.
- **Fix 2** — `evm_utils.py`: Added `send_raw_transaction()` that handles the reth forwarding race (`--sequencer-http` forward completes → sequencer includes tx in block → gossips back to fullnode → fullnode's local pool add sees "already known"). Recovers the tx hash via `keccak256(raw_tx_bytes)`.
- Updated all callers: `test_balance_transfer`, `test_nonce_handling`, `test_tx_forwarding`, `test_transaction_mempool_propagation`, `evm.py`.

## Test plan
- [x] All functional-tests-new pass on CI (PR run)
- [ ] Merge queue passes (the two fixes together eliminate both the nonce contamination and the forwarding race)

payload.title: STR 2042 mempool generalised priority ordering
payload.body:
## Description Generalizes OL mempool transaction ordering behind a pluggable `MempoolPriorityPolicy` trait, while preserving current FIFO behavior unchanged. 1. `MempoolPriorityPolicy` trait (`ordering.rs`) - Associated type `Priority: Ord + Copy + Debug + Send + Sync + 'static`, used as `BTreeMap` keys in the priority index. - `compute_priority(tx, timestamp_micros) -> Self::Priority` computes priority from the transaction and insertion timestamp. `txid` is derived internally to prevent mismatch. 2. `FifoPriority` default implementation Reproduces current timestamp-FIFO semantics via `FifoPriorityKey`. Intrinsic vs extrinsic ordering (`ordering.rs`) - `PackageKey::SnarkAcctUpdate(AccountId)` groups same-account snark transactions that share an intrinsic ordering constraint. - `IntrinsicOrder` with `PartialOrd`, comparable only within the same package (same-account `seq_no`). - `FifoPriorityKey::Ord` applies intrinsic order first, falls back to FIFO timestamp cross-package. 3. `txid` tiebreaker (correctness fix) All `FifoPriorityKey` variants include a `txid` field. Without it, two transactions with the same timestamp would silently overwrite each other in the `BTreeMap`. 4. Transaction ID `compute_txid()` on canonical `OLTransaction` uses SSZ tree-hash over transaction data. Mempool reuses this directly, no bespoke txid computation or manual `TreeHash` impls. 5. payload.title: Executor for generating and broadcasting graph data
payload.body:
## Description

<!--
Provide a brief summary of the changes and the motivation behind them.
-->
This PR implements the executor to generate and broadcast graph data required to produce an operator's graph. This data only includes the outpoint used to fund the claim transaction for now but will probably include adaptor keys as well in the future. The p2p types/services required for this have been updated here and in the spec.

To implement this feature, the BridgeDb trait's `funds`-related method has been split into one for claim and the other for withdrawal fulfillment since the former needs the `GraphIdx` but the latter only needs/has `DepositIdx` as the key. Then, the implementation of the `fund_v3_transaction` in the operator wallet used for funding the withdrawal fulfillment has been updated so that we can construct withdrawal fulfillment transactions deterministically and the executor for it becomes idempotent.

AI was used for generating db tests.

### Type of Change

<!--
Select the type of change your PR introduces (put an `x` in all that apply):

payload.title: Prague Testnet Support Retro
payload.body_md:
## Wins

We got Prague testnet support over the line across the core stack. The biggest win is that `product:strata` node support landed close to plan, despite the number of moving parts across `repo:alpen`, `repo:strata-p2p`, and the downstream public surfaces. person:prajwolrg drove the milestone through the final integration window, with person:MdTeach and person:bewakes helping keep the protocol-side changes moving instead of letting the work fragment into repo-local fixes.

Infra also stabilized enough for the rest of us to validate against something real. person:krsnapaudel carried a lot of the late coordination here, especially where testnet profile assumptions had to be made concrete. That unblocked bridge and explorer work that would otherwise have stayed theoretical.

On the bridge side, person:Rajil1213 and person:ProofOfKeags pushed through validation of `product:strata-bridge` against the live-ish Prague environment. This exposed issues we were unlikely to catch with isolated config review: mismatched chain/testnet parameters, assumptions about service availability, and places where bridge verification depended on infra state being stable longer than our test loops expected.

We also closed the loop on visibility. `repo:checkpoint-explorer`, `repo:alpen-dashboards`, and `repo:alpen-faucet` were not as early as we wanted, but they did become part of the milestone rather than being treated as separate launch chores. person:john-light helped surface the public-facing gaps clearly enough that we could distinguish “core support exists” from “external users can actually use this testnet.”

## Challenges

The main challenge was cross-repo configuration drift. Prague parameters were represented in too many places, and ownership of the canonical testnet profile was unclear. `repo:alpen`, `repo:strata-bridge`, `repo:strata-p2p`, explorer indexing, dashboards, and faucet setup each had some local interpretation of “Prague-ready.” The deltas were often small, but small config mismatches are exactly what make testnet support feel flaky.

Bridge validation depended on late infra stability. That is partly inherent: bridge behavior has to be tested against real services and real indexing paths. But we spent too much of the buffer proving the environment rather than proving the bridge. When infra moved, bridge validation restarted. When explorer indexing lagged, we lost observability. This compressed the final week and made it harder for person:Rajil1213 and person:ProofOfKeags to separate bridge defects from environment defects.

Public polish trailed protocol readiness. We had working core support before we had a clean public checklist, faucet readiness, explorer confidence, and docs that matched the actual deployed profile. That meant the milestone was technically close but operationally noisy. The retro beat from 2026-02-26 to 2026-03-04 captured this accurately: bridge verification and explorer indexing consumed the buffer that had been intended for public polish.

## What we'd do differently

We should define one owner for the testnet profile before implementation starts. That does not mean one person owns every repo, but it does mean one source of truth exists for chain parameters, service endpoints, bootnodes, bridge settings, explorer assumptions, faucet limits, and dashboard labels. For this milestone, ownership emerged through pressure. Next time it should be explicit.

We should treat bridge validation as a first-class milestone dependency, not a final integration task. The bridge is not just a consumer of the testnet; it is one of the best tests of whether the testnet is coherent. person:Rajil1213 and person:ProofOfKeags needed stable infra earlier, and infra needed earlier signal from bridge validation.

We should put public-facing readiness on the same board as core support. Docs, faucet, explorer indexing, and dashboards are not marketing extras for a public testnet. They are part of whether the testnet can be used and debugged. person:john-light should be pulled in earlier with a concrete readiness checklist tied to the deployed profile, not asked to reconcile docs after parameters have already drifted.

## Action items

- Assign a single Prague-style testnet profile owner for each future testnet milestone. Default proposal: protocol driver owns the profile, infra owns deployment realization, bridge signs off on bridge-specific parameters.

- Add a shared config manifest consumed or checked by `repo:alpen`, `repo:strata-bridge`, `repo:strata-p2p`, `repo:checkpoint-explorer`, `repo:alpen-dashboards`, and `repo:alpen-faucet`.

- Create a cross-repo config drift check in CI before the next public testnet cut.

- Move bridge validation earlier in the schedule, with person:Rajil1213 and person:ProofOfKeags validating against a stable staging profile before final infra hardening.

- Require explorer indexing, faucet readiness, dashboards, and public docs to be green before calling testnet support complete.

- Keep person:prajwolrg as the driver for final protocol signoff, but split release readiness into explicit protocol, infra, bridge, and public-surface checklists.

payload.title: STR 1202 Generic MMR database interface
payload.body:
## Description

Replaces the legacy `GlobalMmrDatabase` trait with a storage-only `MmrIndexDatabase` interface, separating MMR algorithm logic from the database layer. Closes the TOCTOU race condition across all MMR read/write paths.

### Before
- `GlobalMmrDatabase` bundled MMR algorithms (append, pop, proof) into the DB trait
- Callers managed `MmrMetadata` manually
- `BitManipulatedMmrAlgorithm` scattered across `db/types` and test harnesses
- Borsh-typed `TypedMmrHandle<T>` coupled serialization to the handle
- Flat-position encoding (`u64`) leaked into public API
- Leaf count derived via binary search — O(log N) point reads per mutation
- Proof generation split across separate validate + count-read + proof-gen DB calls (race-prone)
- Block assembly used per-leaf `get_leaf_blocking` validation loops with 10 MMR-specific error variants

### After
**`MmrIndexDatabase` trait** — storage-only, 5 methods:
- `get_node(mmr_id, NodePos) -> Option<Hash>`
- `get_preimage(mmr_id, LeafPos) -> Option<Vec<u8>>`
- `get_leaf_count(mmr_id) -> u64` — O(1) from dedicated `leaf_count_tree`
- `fetch_node_paths(Vec<MmrNodePos>, preimages) -> MmrNodeTable` — transactional batch read
- `apply_update(MmrBatchWrite) -> ()` — atomic multi-tree transaction with CAS preconditions on leaf count and node hashes

**`NodePos` / `LeafPos`** — structured `(height, index)` types with private fields. No flat-position encoding in the public API.

<!--

* Feature-gate `borsh` and `arbitrary` dependencies in the `zkaleido` crate so they are optional.

payload.title: refactor(asm): narrow Subprotocol trait interface to L1BlockCommitment
payload.body:
## Description

<!--
Provide a brief summary of the changes and the motivation behind them.
-->
* Replaces `AnchorState` with `L1BlockCommitment` in `Subprotocol::process_txs`, since subprotocols cannot parse the full `AnchorState` — it contains opaque state of other subprotocols. Also since the `AsmHistoryAccumulatorState` is used upfront before subprotocol-processing to construct `VerifiedAuxData`, it is not required either. The only piece subprotocols actually need is the L1 block reference being processed.
* Passes `L1BlockCommitment` (as l1ref) into `Subprotocol::process_msgs` in place of `Params`, enabling the bridge subprotocol to use the actual L1 block ID when creating withdrawal assignments instead of a zero placeholder.
* Updates all subprotocol implementations and the ASM STF pipeline to use the narrowed interface.
* Remove redundant docstring and update it for clarity.

payload.title: (btcio/writer): Remove 2x multiplier in fee estimation
payload.body:
## Description

It seems like the issue with excessive fees in signet is because of the existing 2x multiplier in the fee estimation. In signet, the issue most likely unfolds like this.
1. Let the existing fee rate be x.
2. When queried by the fee policy, it would be multiplied by 2 and the fee rate is interpreted as 2x.
3. Transactions are created and submitted to bitcoin with the fee rate of 2x.
4. Once the transactions are accepted, the network's fee rate becomes roughly 2x because signet mostly has empty blocks.
5. When queried by the fee policy it would again be multiplied by 2 and the new fee rate would be interpreted to be 4x, and so on.

This PR removes the 2x multiplier. The query made to `estimatesmartfee` RPC should already be enough because it returns the "conservative" estimation by default(which is slightly higher) than the other option("economical"). See https://chainquery.com/bitcoin-cli/estimatesmartfee.
The PR also adds some logging for observability of the fee rate and actual fee being paid in a transaction.

payload.body:
## Depends On
- This PR is dependent on #105.
- Please rebase this branch after #105 merges before final review/merge.

## Summary
This PR replaces the old state machine scheduler/executor split with a dedicated **SM executor** architecture and stable API surface, then hardens restore, ack, and failure behavior for correctness-first operation.

## What Changed

### 1) Crate and workspace migration
- Added new crates:
  - `crates/sm-executor-api`
  - `crates/sm-executor`
- Removed legacy runtime path:
  - `crates/state-machine/executor/*` (runtime modules deleted)
- Updated workspace wiring/dependencies in `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock`.
- Renamed design doc from scheduler to executor:
  - `docs/sm-scheduler.md` -> `docs/sm-executor.md`

### 2) New public API boundary (`sm-executor-api`)
- Added stable command/config/handle API:
  - `SmExecutorConfig` with bounded command queue + configured `known_peers`
  - `SmCommand` / `SmCommandKind` with role-targeted commands
  - role helpers (`SmRole`, role/payload pairing helpers)
  - `SmExecutorHandle` send interface
- This isolates bridge/RPC from executor internals and monoio/FASM details.

### 3) New executor core (`sm-executor`)
- Implemented single-threaded monoio executor loop with `monoio::select!` over:
  - job completions
  - inbound protocol requests
  - bridge/RPC commands
- Added explicit routing matrices for:
  - protocol msg -> role/input
  - command -> role/input
  - completion -> role/completion
- Added startup restore over

This PR creates a new binary for the bridge-node for v1 by hooking up all the sub-components together. ## Description

<!--
Provide a brief summary of the changes and the motivation behind them.
-->
### Issue

The current client masks error messages coming out of bitcoin-core. For example, when checking if a transaction exists with `get_raw_transaction_*`, the client returns an `InternalServerError(500)` which makes troubleshooting very difficult.

### Root Cause

The errors are being masked at two layers:

1. `src/client/mod.rs` returned `ClientError::Status(...)` immediately for non-2xx HTTP responses, without attempting to parse a JSON-RPC error body.
2. In `src/client/v29.rs`, several methods wrapped `call(...)` errors as `ClientError::Parse(e.to_string())`, which erased typed RPC error classification (`ClientError::Server(code, message)`).

payload.title: refactor(asm): simplify subprotocol trait and params
payload.body:
## Description

<!--
Provide a brief summary of the changes and the motivation behind them.
-->

The Subprotocol trait had a `Params` associated type that was designed to support per-block-height parameter changes, but this capability was never actually used. In practice, `Params` was only ever read during init to construct the initial state, and then threaded through every method signature (`pre_process_txs`, `process_txs`) unused — implementations just ignored them with `_params`.

So this PR removes it. 

- Remove unused `params` and `prestate` arguments from the `Subprotocol::preprocess` method
- Remove unused `params` from `process_txs`, simplifying the subprotocol trait surface
- Make `Subprotocol::init` infallible (returns `Self::State` instead of Result)
- Move `max_seq_no` from admin init config into admin subprotocol state
- Rename `Params` to `InitConfig` across all subprotocols to better reflect their purpose as one-time initialization data rather than runtime parameters
- Rename leftover _params / _genesis field names to _config for consistency

payload.title: STR-2434: use canonical tip as fallback for duty fetcher instead of genesis
payload.body:
## Description

After a node restart where epoch 1+ has been finalized, the sequencer duty fetcher incorrectly uses the genesis block as its starting tip. This prevents the chain from resuming when the fork choice manager (FCM) is initialized with a finalized epoch above genesis.

### Root Cause
`duty_fetcher_worker` polls `status_channel.get_ol_sync_status()` for the current tip. On fresh restart, `StatusChannel` is initialized with `ol_state: None`, so no status is available until FCM processes its first block. The fallback is:
`storage.ol_block().get_canonical_block_at_async(0)  // always returns genesis`

On first-ever startup this is harmless: FCM's finalized epoch defaults to genesis-level, so genesis is the root of its pending_table. A slot 1 block built on top of genesis attaches successfully, FCM publishes a status, and the chain moves forward.

After any restart where epoch 1+ is finalized, FCM initializes with the epoch terminal block (e.g. slot 4) as its pending_table root — genesis is not present. The duty fetcher still falls back to genesis, generates a slot 1 block, and FCM fails to attach it with:
```
error processing block, interpreting as invalid: tried to attach blkid <slot-1-id> but missing parent blkid <genesis-id>
```
No status is ever published, the duty fetcher keeps retrying with genesis, and the chain is stuck.

### Why we didn’t catch this with existing functional tests

payload.title: fix(docker): store master Xpriv in sequencer.key to avoid double derivation
payload.body:
## Summary

`init-keys.sh` was saving the output of `genseqprivkey` (a derived Xpriv at `m/20000'/10'`, depth=2) to `sequencer.key`. Both `genseqpubkey` and `load_seqkey()` call `SequencerKeys::new()` on whatever Xpriv they are given, which derives `m/20000'/10'` internally. This caused double derivation (`m/20000'/10'/20000'/10'`).

The fix copies the master Xpriv (`sequencer.bin`, depth=0) directly to `sequencer.key`, so the single derivation in `load_seqkey()` and `genseqpubkey` produces the correct key.

[STR-2537](https://alpenlabs.atlassian.net/browse/STR-2537)

payload.title: storage: add FoundationDB backend and async state acquisition
payload.body:
## Summary
This PR introduces a FoundationDB-backed state storage provider and updates the storage-provider API to support async, fallible state-handle acquisition. It also propagates those API changes through the SM executor and job executors.

## Dependency
This PR is stacked on top of #108 (`feat(sm-executor): replace SM scheduler with SM executor + API crate, restore/ack hardening`) and should not be merged before that PR lands.

## Why
FDB-backed state sessions need async setup and can fail during acquisition. The previous sync, infallible provider interface was too restrictive for real backends.

## What changed
- add new `mosaic-storage-fdb` crate
- wire the crate and `foundationdb` dependency into the workspace
- make `StorageProvider` and `StorageProviderMut` state acquisition async and fallible
- update in-memory and kvstore providers to satisfy the new API
- forward `Commit` through kvstore-backed state handles
- update SM executor restore and execution paths to handle storage acquisition failures explicitly
- update job executors to await storage acquisition and map failures to retry/storage-unavailable outcomes
- implement FoundationDB directory-layer scoping under `global_path + ["mosaic", "v1"] + <peer>/<role>`
- implement `FdbTransaction` as `KvStore + Commit`
- make FDB range scans lazy and paged rather than full-buffered
- use native FDB `clear_range` for efficient range deletes
- cache peer/role directory prefixes in memory to avoid repeated directory round

## Description

<!--
Provide a brief summary of the changes and the motivation behind them.

`EvenPublicKey::arbitrary` could fail with `IncorrectFormat` when random bytes happened to exceed the secp256k1 curve order or be zero. Fix by clamping the secret key bytes to guarantee validity. payload.title: feat: add mosaic binary and lifecycle wiring
payload.body:
## Summary
Adds the main `mosaic` binary and associated wiring to compose the core runtime components into a single daemon. This also hardens component lifecycle/shutdown semantics, improves operational tracing in the main loops, adds production-oriented table-store publish semantics, and includes a small helper binary for deriving peer IDs from signing keys.

## Stack / Dependencies
- This PR is stacked on top of #111.
- It should be reviewed and merged after #111.
- Follow-up protocol work remains in #117 for explicit garbling-table receipt acknowledgement.

## What Changed
- Added the main daemon binary under `bin/mosaic`.
- Added `mosaic-peer-id` helper binary for generating or inspecting peer IDs from Ed25519 signing keys.
- Added TOML-based config loading for the daemon.
- Restricted daemon state storage to FoundationDB-backed storage.
- Added table-store backend support for:
  - local filesystem
  - S3-compatible object stores
- Added local multi-node example configs under `bin/mosaic/config/`.
- Switched the main binary to `monoio` and `mimalloc`.

## Lifecycle / Shutdown
- Introduced explicit shutdown controllers for:
  - SM executor
  - job scheduler
- Updated daemon shutdown ordering to stop ingress before executor/scheduler teardown.
- Removed reliance on dropped handles / accidental channel closure for process shutdown.

## Storage Safety
- Hardened S3/object-store publish semantics for garbling tables.
- Tables now publish through immutable versioned paths plus

payload.body:
## Description

<!--
Provide a brief summary of the changes and the motivation behind them.
-->
This PR addresses an issue reported via our bug-bounty program. The issue (taken from the report):

> The function `is_counterproof_nack_tx` in `crates/bridge-sm/src/tx_classifier.rs` contains two logic errors that cause NACK transactions to be attributed to the wrong operator.
> The function's purpose is to identify which operator posted a NACK against a counterproof transaction. It does this by inspecting the NACK transaction's inputs to find which counterproof output is being spent, then mapping that back to an operator index.
> 
> `is_counterproof_nack_tx` never captures the counterproof summary’s array index. Inside the outer `find_map`, it returns `input_index` from `tx.input.iter().enumerate()` (`crates/bridge-sm/src/tx_classifier.rs`). This is merely the position of the spending input inside the NACK transaction, not the operator slot. Consequently, whichever input happens to spend the counterproof output dictates `nacker_idx`, so operators are routinely misattributed when the broadcaster reorders inputs.
>
> ```rust
> tx.input.iter().enumerate().find_map(|(input_index, txin)| {
>     if txin.previous_output == expected_counteproof_outpoint {
>         Some(input_index as OperatorIdx)
>     } else {
>         None
>     }
> })

> The remapping that follows inverts the pov_idx adjustment. Because the counterproof array omits the POV operator, a counterproof entry at position

payload.title: fix!(strata): use sequencer config for poll interval
payload.body:
## Description

The OL sequencer in `strata` was producing blocks every 1 second instead of respecting the configured `sequencer.ol_block_time_ms` in the `sequencer.toml` config file. The` --duty-poll-interval/-i` CLI flag defaulted to `1_000`ms, and this poll interval drove the `SequencerTimerInput` tick rate. During chain startup/catchup, all block target timestamps are in the past, so every tick produced a block immediately -- making the poll interval the effective block time.

This removes the `--duty-poll-interval/-i` CLI flag and instead derives the sequencer service tick interval from `ol_block_time_ms` in the sequencer runtime config (`sequencer.toml`).

payload.title: STR 2559 add RPC support for tip block epoch
payload.body:
## Description

- Replace `tip` from `OLBlockCommitment` (slot + blkid) with `RpcOLBlockInfo` (blkid, slot, epoch, is_terminal) in `getChainStatus`
- Drop `parent`/`latest` epoch field — completed epoch is derivable from `tip.epoch`
- Enrich `ChainSyncStatus` with `tip_epoch` and `tip_is_terminal` so the RPC handler avoids a DB read per call
- Update EE side, functional tests, and OpenRPC schema test

## Motivation

The old `tip` was just a block commitment with no epoch info. Consumers needed the `parent` field to know which epoch the chain was in. By enriching `tip` with epoch and terminal info, `parent` becomes redundant — `tip.epoch - 1` gives the completed epoch (or `tip.epoch` on a terminal block).

## Wire-shape change

`getChainStatus` response changes:
- `tip`: `{slot, blkid}` → `{blkid, slot, epoch, is_terminal}`
- `parent` field removed
- `confirmed` and `finalized` unchanged

This PR was created with help from Claude Code and Codex.

Updated callers, tests and functional tests to use new fields.

payload.title: 1877 da by re execution
payload.body:
## Description
                                                                                              
The PR does the following:
  - Reconstruct DA data by re-executing epoch blocks from the epoch boundary rather than    persisting diffs. Cache accumulated DA per block in an `EpochDaTracker`, evicting stale parent entries to bound memory.
  - Thread `AccumulatedDaData` (state diff accumulator + epoch logs) as a single unit through the block assembly pipeline, replacing the previous split handling of accumulator and logs.
  - Enforce checkpoint payload size limits during block assembly. After each successful     transaction, check the estimated checkpoint size against both component-level limits (DA diff, log count, total log payload) and the combined L1 envelope limit (395 KB). Signal epoch sealing at 90% of any limit and hard-reject transactions that would exceed any limit. This ensures checkpoints never exceed what `CheckpointSidecar::new()` accepts or what can be posted in a single L1 envelope.
  - Introduce shared checkpoint size validation in `checkpoint-types-ssz`. `LogMetrics` tracks log dimensions incrementally; `checkpoint_size_verdict()` checks all dimensions with soft/hard thresholds; `validate_checkpoint_components()` provides hard-limit validation for `CheckpointSidecar` construction. Block assembly and checkpoint builder now share a single source of truth for size limits.
  - Fix epoch DA rebuild bug where execute_block_batch received the first ep

## Description

~~This PR is **VERY INCOMPLETE**.~~

This cleans up a bunch of issues that escaped notice with the tx types, especially meshing the chain types with the snark account update types.  This more cleanly splits out the accumulator proofs that accompany update data into a separate structure as part of the full transaction, so that we can define a "txid" concept independently.  There was a pretty significant issue where we separately describe the entry hash in an accumulator *twice*, once in the claim and once in the proof.  This makes it easy for us to accidentally check one value but use a different one, when the value should simply not be provided twice.

Unfortunately this is quite more complicated than I anticipated, as it touches multiple crates ~~and I haven't even gotten done finishing the main change itself yet!~~ I have finished the main changes and all the downstream consequences.  There's still some cleanup I could do but it's in a good state.

**Changes include:**

* moving `MessageEntry` to `strata-acct-types`
* using `RawMerkleProof` in more places
* defining more parts of snark update txs in `strata-ol-chain-types-new`

payload.body:
## Summary
- Adds `--checkpoint-predicate` flag (`always-accept` | `sp1-groth16`) to both `genparams` and `gen-asm-params` subcommands
- When omitted, existing feature-gated behavior is preserved (backwards compatible)
- Docker `init-keys.sh` and functional test `datatool.py` now explicitly pass `--checkpoint-predicate always-accept`

This is created with Claude code

## Context
The M2 development cluster was deployed with `Sp1Groth16` checkpoint predicate (because datatool was built with `-F sp1-builder`) when `AlwaysAccept` was intended. This caused the ASM to reject all checkpoints, permanently stalling at epoch 0. The root cause is that predicate selection was compile-time only with no runtime override.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo check --bin strata-datatool` passes (without `sp1-builder`)
- [x] `cargo clippy --bin strata-datatool --all-features` passes
- [ ] CI passes
- [ ] Verify `strata-datatool genparams --checkpoint-predicate always-accept` produces `"checkpoint_predicate": "AlwaysAccept"` in output
- [ ] Verify `strata-datatool gen-asm-params --checkpoint-predicate always-accept ...` produces `AlwaysAccept` in ASM params

payload.title: feat!(ssz): finish ASM serialization migration
payload.body:
## Summary
This PR finishes the remaining ASM-side SSZ migration work and updates the pinned `alpen` dependency to the helper commit needed to complete it.

It does these things:

- bumps `moho` to the non-Borsh SSZ version
- bumps `alpen`/`typed-sled` for the SSZ + `rkyv`-compatible dependency set
- converts the remaining ASM-local payloads, messages, and subprotocol state from Borsh-first encodings to native SSZ
- replaces the last direct ASM calls to legacy Borsh decoding in the `checkpoint-v0` path with helper APIs exposed from `alpen`
- removes stale Borsh-based decoding in the runner and drops now-unused Borsh dependencies from migrated crates

## Remaining Borsh
This branch no longer uses Borsh directly for ASM-local bridge/admin/checkpoint payloads, messages, or state.

The only remaining Borsh in this repo is compatibility glue for:

- `AnchorState`
- `AuxData`
- ASM manifest/log wrapper types

Those shims still exist because the current `alpen` storage/state layer still uses Borsh-backed DB codecs for ASM values. Removing them entirely requires a follow-up in `alpen` storage/state rather than more local ASM migration.

## Dependency Note
This PR now pins `alpen` to commit `ee8ab446f26ee451e2f7b878b4acad3f95c3339d` from `refactor/ssz-asm`, which adds the helper APIs needed for:

- raw `RawBitcoinTx` byte access
- legacy `SignedCheckpoint` / `Checkpoint` decoding
- legacy checkpoint proof output decoding
- legacy `Chainstate` decoding

## Notes To Reviewers

payload.body:
## Description

`asm_params.py` imports `ASM_MAGIC_BYTES` from `constants` at module load time:

```python
# functional-tests/factory/common/asm_params.py
from constants import ASM_MAGIC_BYTES
```

Commit `0f6cc31d` introduced `functional-tests/constants.py` and updated `asm_params.py` to import from it, but did not add the corresponding `COPY` instruction to `docker/asm-runner/Dockerfile`. As a result, any fresh container build (ECR, CI, Kubernetes) crashes immediately on startup:

```
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'constants'
```

This PR adds the one missing `COPY` line so the full import chain resolves at runtime.

payload.body:
## Description

<!--
Provide a brief summary of the changes and the motivation behind them.
-->
Currently, the gossipsub protocol only propagates the authenticated raw message to downstream consumers and not the sender. This impedes the consumers' ability to validate whether the sender is even allowed to send the message and whether that message should be accepted. The way this is being resolved now is that the payload itself is also signed but there is a possibility that there is an identity discontinuity (the outer sender and inner sender may be different, and/or additional downsteam checks may be missing as is the case now). In general, it is a good practice to not manage two different keys/auth contexts for the same message. So this PR changes the `GossipEvent` to also include the sender's public key.

AI was used to make the necessary changes.

payload.body:
## Description

Adds `batch_verify_shares` to `vs3/` which verifies multiple (PolynomialCommitment, &[Share]) pairs in a single MSM via RLC. Instead of evaluating each committed polynomial individually (174 EC scalar muls per share), it aggregates scalar coefficients per commitment point using cheap field arithmetic, then checks the combined equation in one MSM. The evaluator's `handle_verify_opened_input_shares` is updated to use this, replacing the triple-nested verify_share loop. This brings down runtime for verifying shares in the e2e test (see stf PRs) from 1h to 1min.

## Description

The SSZ-defined `MAX_LOGS_PER_BLOCK` (4096) existed in chain-types but was
never enforced at runtime. Log collection used unbounded `Vec<OLLog>` in all
paths.

### Changes

**Primitives** (`ol/chain-types`, `ol/stf`)
- Re-export `MAX_LOGS_PER_BLOCK` from `strata_ol_chain_types_new`

- Enforce after tx segment processing, after manifest processing, and before

- Enforce before logs-root comparison / final state-root check
- `verify_epoch_preseal_with_diff` excluded (no log collection)

payload.title: fix(alpen-ee): suppress duplicate EE update submissions
payload.body:
## Description

This fixes the EE sequencer repeatedly submitting the same `SnarkAccountUpdate` while the OL account `seq_no` is unchanged.

The main changes are:

- add local pending submission state in the update submitter so the same head batch is not re-submitted until OL advances or the retry window expires
- keep the existing cached-update path, but separate "cached update" from "already submitted and waiting on OL"
- reduce redundant OL tracker notifications by only notifying watchers when finalized status or consensus heads actually change, and only once per extend cycle
- add focused tests for duplicate suppression, retry-after-backoff, and immediate progress once OL `seq_no` advances

This keeps the existing safety net of OL mempool dedupe, but stops relying on it as the primary way to suppress duplicate submissions.

AI assistance notice: I used AI tooling to help investigate the retry path, draft the change, and validate the affected test/lint flow. The final changes were reviewed and verified with targeted tests and workspace checks.

payload.title: perf: add L1 block body verification with tx inclusion proofs
payload.body:
## Description

<!--
Provide a brief summary of the changes and the motivation behind them.
-->
Originally, we were using the following to check the validity of the bitcoin block body.
```rust
assert!(block.check_merkle_root() && block.check_witness_commitment());
```
While this works, this is really expensive for a full block because of the two main reasons:
1. ZkVMs have precompiles for RustCrypto sha2 function can't be used inside of the bitcoin because it's using sha2 from bitcoin-hashes instead.
2. Verifying the inclusion of the witness commitment in a coinbase transaction is sufficient instead of computing the merkle tree root again.

So in this PR:
1. Add coinbase Merkle inclusion proof (TxidInclusionProof) so SegWit blocks verify the coinbase against the Merkle root without recomputing the full tree — significant performance gain for ZK proof generation on large blocks.
2. Centralize SHA-256d operations (`compute_txid`, `compute_wtxid`, `calculate_root`) using RustCrypto's SHA-2 instead of the bitcoin crate internals, enabling SP1/Risc0 ZK prover acceleration via patched crates.
3. Extract error types into dedicated errors.rs with new L1BodyError enum and proper error propagation through AsmError::InvalidL1Body instead of panics.
4. Localize `strata-btc-verification` as a workspace crate (was an external git dependency)
 

### Type of Change

-->

payload.title: STR 2183 Use service framework for the btcio broadcaster
payload.body:
## Description

Migrate L1 broadcaster to the `strata-service` framework, replacing the raw `tokio::select!` loop in `broadcaster_task` with the `AsyncService` trait, matching the pattern used by other services in the codebase.

* `TickingInput<TokioMpscInput<_>>` merges periodic ticks with command input; if the command input closes, `recv_next` returns `None` and the broadcaster service exits. This intentionally changes prior behavior: the old `broadcaster_task` tolerated command-channel closure and continued polling on ticks.
* `put_tx_entry` now fails fast when storage returns no index, with `BroadcasterError::MissingEntryIndex(txid)` instead of silently continuing. The DB write stays on the caller's task; the service receives a fire-and-forget `NotifyNewEntry`.
* `alpen-client` gains a `TaskManager`/`TaskExecutor` lifecycle for btcio tasks; it previously spawned the broadcaster future directly on tokio.

This PR was created with help from Codex and Claude Code.

test(orchestrator): capture graph data sender-identity regression

Tests that GraphDataExchange messages from unknown senders and from
senders whose resolved operator index does not match graph_idx.operator
are rejected. These tests intentionally fail against the current
(unfixed) code to document the missing check.

fix(orchestrator): verify sender identity for GraphDataExchange

The GraphDataExchange classifier accepted graph data from any peer
without checking that the sender's resolved operator index matches
the graph_idx.operator claimed in the message. A malicious peer could
impersonate another operator's graph data.

Now looks up the sender via the operator table and rejects the message
if the sender is unknown or does not match the claimed operator.

payload.title: fix(orchestrator): verify sender identity for GraphDataExchange
payload.body:
## Description

<!--
Provide a brief summary of the changes and the motivation behind them.
-->
The GraphDataExchange classifier accepted graph data from any peer without checking that the p2p sender's resolved operator index matched the `graph_idx.operator` claimed in the message. A malicious peer could impersonate another operator's graph data. In this fix, we first look up the sender via the operator table and then reject the message if the sender is unknown or does not match the claimed operator. This is similar to how the `PayoutDescriptorExchange` message is validated.

Claude was used to generate the regression test in the first commit.

payload.title: docker: make it possible to volume-mount asm-params
payload.body:
## Description

<!--
Provide a brief summary of the changes and the motivation behind them.
-->
This PR updates the `gen_asm_params.py` script and the entrypoint script for `asm-runner` container such that the `asm-params.json` file can be volume-mounted and updated from outside the container. Earlier, the entire file was auto-generated by the container based on the bridge's `params.toml` and some default values set in the functional tests (as they shared the same generator function). This has been updated so that the passed `asm-params.json` file is now updated in-place (so that the genesis L1 view is accurate). The rest of the values in the file are kept intact but cross-checked against the passed bridge `params.toml` file at container startup for common fields (`recovery_delay`, `operator_fee`, etc.).

Note that the `compose.yml` file does not volume mount the params and instead copies it over into the container since the sample params file is tracked by git and we don't want each container run (which updates the params file) to introduce a git diff.

I've tested these changes by running the docker stack locally and updating any configuration files along the way to make sure that the fulfillments work. I've also updated the `checkpoint` recipe in `.justfile` with the new `dev-cli` invocation.

Claude was used to update the scripts.

## Description

<!--
Provide a brief summary of the changes and the motivation behind them.
-->
This PR adds the following new RPCs:

**Data Availability RPCs (StrataBridgeDaApi)**

  - `graphData(graph_idx)` — Returns the `GraphSMCtx`, `SetupParams`, and `DepositParams` needed to reconstruct a game graph externally. Available once the graph has been generated.
  - `aggregateSignatures(graph_idx)` — Returns the aggregate Schnorr signatures needed to finalize presigned graph transactions. Available once the graph has been signed. This is a flattened list of signatures that can be unpacked with the `GameFunctor`.

**Monitoring RPCs (StrataBridgeMonitoringApi)**

  - `pendingWithdrawals()` — Lists deposit indices that have an active withdrawal (i.e., an assigned operator and the deposit unwithdrawn).
  - `pendingWithdrawalInfo(deposit_idx)` — Returns structured info about a pending withdrawal, split into:
    - `assigned_operator` — the operator assigned to fulfill the withdrawal
    - `assigned_claim` — the assigned operator's active claim, if any
    - `competing_claims` — claims from non-assigned operators (faulty by definition)

  Each `RpcActiveClaim` includes:
    - `operator` / `claim_txid` — who claimed and which tx
    - `fulfilled` — whether the operator fulfilled the withdrawal before claiming (derived from `fulfillment_txid` in the graph state)
    - `phase` — where the claim sits in the challenge-response game (`Claimed`, `Contested`, `BridgeProofPosted`, `BridgePro

payload.title: Pull-based table transfer orchestration
payload.body:
## Description

Replace push-based garbling table transfer with an explicit request/receipt protocol. The evaluator now drives the transfer: it sends a `TableTransferRequest` for each table it needs, the garbler transfers only on request, and the evaluator acknowledges each table with a `TableTransferReceipt`. Both state machines transition to SetupComplete once all tables are accounted for.

**Protocol changes:**
New wire messages: `TableTransferRequestMsg`, `TableTransferReceiptMsg` (both keyed by GarblingTableCommitment instead of circuit index)
Garbler no longer auto-pushes tables after challenge response; waits for evaluator requests
`WaitForTableTransferReceipt` step removed from garbler — receipt tracking merged into `TransferringGarblingTables`

**Restore behavior:**
Evaluator re-sends requests for unreceived tables and receipts for already-received ones
Garbler is passive on restore — waits for evaluator-driven recovery

**Edge-case fix: transient bulk-stream setup failure**
The garbler's open_bulk_sender can race with the evaluator registering its bulk expectation (ReceiveGarblingTable). Previously this was a common failure mode, but with pull-based transfer the window is narrow (evaluator sends request and registers receive nearly simultaneously). The failure was mapped to SetupFailed (permanent), dropping the action entirely. Added CircuitError::TransientFailure so the garbling coordinator retries on the next pass instead. The e2e test retry loop rep

## Description

Change artifacts/g16.v5c circuit. The new circuit's output is solely dictated by lsb of deposit_id.

steps to generate v5c file:
1. clone: g16 repo and switch to branch `test/simple_circuit_postaudit_smallest`
`test/simple_circuit_postaudit_smallest` branch generates sample ckt meant for test purposes only.
The binary circuit's function is defined [here](https://github.com/alpenlabs/g16/blob/test/simple_circuit_postaudit_smallest/g16ckt/src/gadgets/groth16.rs#L539)
In summary: 
```
combine_all_wires <- AND(all_wires) // we use up all input wires
wire_a <-XOR(combine_all_wires, combine_all_wires) // wire_a is now always zero
output_wire <-  wire_a  OR deposit_id_lsb // result is dependent only on deposit_id_lsb
```


2. generate v5a ckt file: cd g16gen && cargo run generate 6 && cargo run write-input-bits 6
3. clone: ckt repo
4. move g16gen/g16.ckt file to ckt/lvl/
5. generate v5c file: cd crates/lvl && cargo run prealloc g16.ckt g16.v5c

payload.title: fix(docker): chmod +x binaries in runtime stage to fix Permission denied on macOS buildx
payload.body:
## Summary

When building on macOS (arm64) with `docker buildx` targeting `linux/amd64`, `COPY --from=builder` does not reliably preserve the executable bit. This causes a `Permission denied` crash at container startup on EKS:

```
/usr/local/bin/entrypoint.sh: 7: /usr/local/bin/strata-bridge: Permission denied
```

Fix: explicit `chmod +x` in the runtime stage of both Dockerfiles.

## Changes

**`docker/strata-bridge/Dockerfile`**
```dockerfile
RUN chmod +x /usr/local/bin/strata-bridge /usr/local/bin/entrypoint.sh
```

**`docker/asm-runner/Dockerfile`**
```dockerfile
RUN chmod +x /usr/local/bin/strata-asm-runner /usr/local/bin/entrypoint.sh
```

## Test plan

- [ ] Build both images on macOS with `docker buildx --platform linux/amd64`
- [ ] Verify containers start without `Permission denied`
- [ ] Confirm on Linux native builds still work (chmod is a no-op there)

payload.title: Refactor: use of i64 and db swap
payload.body:
In this pr I have attempted to fix an ugly semantic flaw we had in our codebase due to a limitation of Postgres. Pg does not support U64, so we translated u64 (block height, checkpoint idx, etc) to i64 and vice versa which added unnecessary application level complication throughout the code. 
So the major changes are: 
- removal of PGU64 abstraction which used to do i64<->u64 translations.
- use of mariadb instead of pg
- removal of separate migration service to avoid deployment complication. Now the migration will be handled by backend at the startup.
- have added func-tests by following our `alpen` repo, this test sets up a mock strata fullnode and ckpt-exp backend and mostly tests if it is serving through our major routes (`/search`, `/checkpoint?p=<x>` and `/`). This was mostly written by Claude so I do not want it to be critically reviewed. Yet its good to have an eye.
- hooked func-tests to ci.yml workflow

I have tested locally by running `docker compose up --build -d` and also by running `cd functional-tests && ./run-tests.sh`

PS: We have done some additional works which were not planned but felt worthwhile after a few rounds of reviews.
- we have added ci workflows for lints and `just` recipes.
- added functional tests
- updated readme so that anybody can run this project easily.
- removed sentinel values for status and txid with proper enums and option.

payload.title: bitcoind-async-client 0.4 rollout retrospective
payload.body_md:
## Wins

The `bitcoind-async-client` 0.4 rollout put the Strata node path in a materially better place. The main win was not any single RPC wrapper, but the fact that we stopped treating bitcoind as a mostly-stable local dependency and started modeling it as an external service with restarts, partial availability, slow responses, and stateful wallet behavior.

person:krsnapaudel drove this from the infra side and kept the crate focused on operational reality instead of just API coverage. The timeout work was the clearest example: it delayed the initial release target, but it gave protocol callers a safer failure mode than hanging node tasks or relying on ad hoc caller-side cancellation. That tradeoff was correct.

The protocol-side feedback loop improved over the cycle. person:prajwolrg, person:MdTeach, person:delbonis, person:storopoli, person:bewakes, and person:alexhui01 helped expose where the crate API was leaking operational concerns into Strata callers, especially around retry boundaries, startup sequencing, and what errors should be considered transient. We ended up with clearer behavior for the code that actually consumes the client in `alpen` and `strata-common`, not just a cleaner crate in isolation.

Observability also moved forward. The dashboards and operational notes were not glamorous, but they closed a real gap: when a Strata node has degraded bitcoind connectivity, we now have better signals for distinguishing RPC latency, restart windows, and caller misuse. person:alexhui01 joining late in B11 and picking up dashboard polish was useful precisely because they had to learn the historical decisions cold. The onboarding material that came out of that process is better than the scattered notes we had before.

## Challenges

The ownership boundary stayed messy. The crate is infra-owned, but many of the sharp edges only appear in protocol-owned callers. That meant review priorities were often split: infra wanted to harden the client, while protocol reviewers were already loaded with core Strata milestone work. We got through it, but the process depended too much on individual availability and context-sharing.

Regtest mocks repeatedly hid production-like bitcoind restart behavior. The test setup was good enough to validate request/response correctness, but not good enough to reveal lifecycle issues. This showed up most clearly around restart timing, wallet readiness, and assumptions about RPC availability immediately after process recovery. We caught these, but later than we should have.

The timeout work created schedule pressure. In hindsight, that was a predictable conflict: safer behavior required changing expectations in callers, and caller changes are where review cost appears. We treated timeout semantics as an implementation detail for too long, when they were actually part of the operational contract.

Observability competed with milestone review bandwidth. Nobody disagreed that metrics and dashboards mattered, but they were easy to defer because they did not block local correctness. That created a late-cycle pileup where operational documentation, dashboard cleanup, and onboarding notes all converged in B11.

Remaining wallet RPC cleanup was deferred. That was the right call for release focus, but it leaves a known area where the client still carries some historical unevenness.

## What we'd do differently

We would define the crate contract earlier, with protocol callers in the room. Specifically: timeout semantics, retry ownership, transient versus terminal errors, and startup readiness should have been written down before implementation stabilized. That would have reduced review churn and made the release risk more explicit.

We would add restart-oriented tests before relying on regtest mocks for confidence. Mocked RPC tests are still valuable, but they should not be our main evidence for node operations behavior. A small production-like harness that exercises bitcoind restart, delayed wallet readiness, and in-flight request failure would have caught several issues earlier.

We would separate release blockers from operational follow-through more cleanly. Dashboard polish and onboarding docs do not need to block the crate release, but they do need owners and dates. Leaving them as “after the milestone” work made them easier to compress into the end of the cycle.

We would also onboard late-cycle contributors through decision records, not chat archaeology. person:alexhui01’s ramp exposed how much context was implicit. The resulting docs helped, but the cost came after decisions had already been made.

## Action items

- person:krsnapaudel: write and maintain the `bitcoind-async-client` operational contract covering timeout, retry, startup, and error classification semantics.
- person:MdTeach and person:prajwolrg: review protocol caller assumptions against that contract and remove caller-side behavior that duplicates or contradicts the client.
- person:bewakes and person:alexhui01: finish converting B11 operational notes into onboarding material for future node-client work.
- person:storopoli and person:delbonis: identify the minimum restart-oriented test harness needed beyond regtest mocks.
- person:krsnapaudel: file scoped follow-up issues for the deferred wallet RPC cleanup, with release impact labeled explicitly.
- person:alexhui01: keep dashboard polish tied to concrete operational questions, especially bitcoind restart windows, RPC latency, and readiness failures.

payload.title: STR 2560 Add RPC support for get checkpoint info
payload.body:
## Description

Implement OL `getCheckpointInfo` end-to-end with typed confirmation status and tx confirmation count, plus focused RPC/OpenRPC coverage.

### Changes

- Extended ASM v1 `CheckpointTipUpdate` log to carry checkpoint `txid`, and wired CSM persistence.
- Unified `OLCheckpointL1ObservationEntry` into `CheckpointL1Ref` across DB traits, sled store, storage manager, CSM worker, and dbtool.
- Added OL checkpoint RPC types:
  - `RpcCheckpointInfo`
  - `RpcCheckpointL1Ref { l1_block, txid, wtxid }`
  - `RpcCheckpointConfStatus`: `Pending`, `Confirmed { l1_reference, tx_confirmations }`, `Finalized { l1_reference, tx_confirmations }`
- Added OL API method `strata_getCheckpointInfo(epoch: Epoch)`.
- Wired implementation in `bin/strata` provider/server:
  - Builds `l2_range` by walking block ancestry from terminal to find first epoch block.
  - Builds `l1_range` from `prev_summary.new_l1.height + 1` to `cur_summary.new_l1`, fetching the L1 manifest for the start block ID.
  - Derives confirmation status from CSM sync status (`finalized_epoch`).
  - Computes `tx_confirmations = tip_height - observed_height + 1` at read time.
- `wtxid` is temporarily mirrored from `txid` until follow-up STR-2952.

This PR was created with help from Codex and Claude Code.

Bumps [reth-evm-ethereum](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth) from v1.9.1 to v1.11.3.
Release notes

Sourced from reth-evm-ethereum's releases.

Reth v1.11.3

Latest Release

[!IMPORTANT] This release replaces v1.11.x, and users must upgrade to v1.11.3

  • fix(trie): panic in sparse trie proof workers

Update Steps

Nodes can be restarted using the new binary with no required update steps. Errors during payload validation may continue to be seen, but will not stall the node.

To fully fix errors such as those described in issue 22973, shut down the node and run:

reth db --datadir <datadir> repair-trie

This command will take up to 2 hours to complete for ethereum mainnet. Once complete, start reth node as normal.

Update Priority

This table provides priorities for which classes of users should update particular components.

User Class Priority
Payload Builders High
Non-Payload Builders High

payload.title: refactor: decouple StrataAsmSpec from AsmParams and replace GenesisL1View with L1Anchor
payload.body:
## Description

<!--
Provide a brief summary of the changes and the motivation behind them.
-->
`StrataAsmSpec` was responsible for two distinct things: defining the subprotocol pipeline order, and initializing genesis state from `AsmParams`. Genesis initialization is a one-time operation that only happens at chain start, yet it forced every consumer of the spec to carry AsmParams just to construct it. This meant `AsmParams` had to be embedded in the zkVM guest ELF via `env!("ASM_PARAMS_JSON")`, making the ELF depend on deployment-specific parameters even though the guest only needs to know the subprotocol order to execute state transitions.

This PR separates the two concerns: genesis construction moves to a standalone `construct_genesis_state(params)` function, and the spec becomes a stateless unit struct that only declares which subprotocols run and in what order. With params no longer threaded through the spec, the Loader trait and its load_subprotocols method disappear entirely — subprotocol loading now reuses the same Stage dispatch as every other pipeline phase, and `AsmSpec` is reduced to a single method (`call_subprotocols`).

#### Deployment-independent guest ELF

The SP1 guest no longer needs ASM_PARAMS_JSON at compile time. The build script drops all ASM_PARAMS_JSON handling — no env propagation, no skip-if-missing logic. The guest entry point simply calls process_asm_stf(&Sp1ZkVmEnv) with no spec argument, and `StrataAsmSpec` is instantiated internally
payload.head: STR-2936-decouple-strata-asm-spec-from-params

payload.title: Feat: switch system for affine map over primorial via CRT decomposition
payload.body:
## Description

- Extended `word_to_ring` and `hot_to_ring` to compute `a·g(x) + b` (scaling + offset) instead of just `g(x)`.                                                  
- Added CRT infrastructure: `CrtParams` for chunking/working-modulus derivation, Garner's algorithm for reconstruction, and supporting modular arithmetic (`pow2_mod`, `mulmod128`, `mod_inverse`). Used algorithms and pseudocode provided [here](https://cp-algorithms.com/algebra/garners-algorithm.html) as reference. 
- Implemented the affine switch system `build_s_aff`: given an n-bit input x and S coefficient pairs (a, b), evaluates all S affine maps a·x + b in Z_M by chunking, free accumulation, and per-prime residue evaluation.
- Replace floating-point `log2().ceil()` with integer-only `ilog2` and `div_ceil` throughout                                                                                   
- Tested affine map correctness over 10th primorial.

payload.body:
## Summary

- The daily EEST CI has been failing because `init-alpen-client-keys.sh` was renamed to `init-network.sh` in #1476, but the `staging-eest.yml` workflow was never updated.
- Instead of wiring up `init-network.sh` (which requires building `datatool`), this commits static regtest test keys directly — the EEST workflow only runs `alpen-client --dummy-ol-client` and doesn't need full network init.

**Changes:**
- Remove broken "Generate alpen-client keys" step from `staging-eest.yml`
- Commit `docker/.env.alpen-client` with static regtest env vars
- Commit `docker/configs/alpen-client/seq-p2p.hex` P2P key
- Update `docker/.gitignore` to allow only `seq-p2p.hex` through

## Test plan
- [ ] Verify the EEST workflow passes by triggering it manually (`workflow_dispatch`)
- [ ] Confirm no secrets or non-test keys are committed (all values are regtest-only, key derivation verified locally)
